brief.headline: Push to a maker's price: they resell 100% (no manufacturing), so their price includes a margin we can cut out by going direct or pressing them down toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut toward the lower end of the market band — ₹0.65–0.80/pc at our volume — because they resell everything and carry a middleman margin.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc (the 'modest headroom' market range at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: Market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. They manufacture 0.0% and trade 100.0% — so their price includes a reseller margin. We want the maker's price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: No change needed — we already pay in 30 days, and they themselves take 105 days to pay their own suppliers, far longer than similar firms (57 days). Our terms are already fair.

brief.financialLeverage: They're fragile but not desperate: money-health score is 2/10, they're in the grey zone (1.58 Altman Z), and they keep only 2.8% profit on every ₹100 sold. But their cash isn't stuck — it cycles in just 1 day, much faster than similar firms (59 days) — so they can pay bills. We're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue, a meaningful customer. Push hard on price (it's a reseller margin, not their cost), but don't squeeze so hard you tip a weak supplier over — line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a backup first.

evidence.point: They resell everything — no manufacturing — so their price includes a middleman margin we can cut out
Market pricing for a 28 mm PP cap shows room to go lower at higher volume
evidence.figure: Ask band: ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: We're a big customer — over 1% of everything they sell
evidence.figure: Our ₹65.27 L is 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Their money-health score is very weak, a supply risk
evidence.figure: Probe42 score: 2/10, health C (55/100), grey zone (1.58 Altman Z)

evidence.point: Thin profit margin means less room to cut, but it's reseller margin, not manufacturing cost
evidence.figure: They keep 2.8% profit vs 3.1% for similar firms

evidence.point: They have a pending legal case on file

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate and a direct manufacturer.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) making pails, containers, pharma packaging — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A manufacturer lead from public research (India-Pan, medium confidence) — verify capability and willingness to supply pharma-grade rigid packaging before sending an RFQ.

risks: Their money-health is weak (2/10, grey zone) and they have a pending legal case — don't put all our rigid-packaging eggs in this basket; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
They keep only 2.8% profit, so if we push too hard on price and they're already stretched, supply could wobble — balance the squeeze with a clear backup plan.
100% of their revenue is resale, not manufacturing — if their own source dries up or raises price, they have no factory to fall back on, and our supply stops.
We have no internal best-price benchmark for rigid plastic packaging in our own data — the market ask is our only guide, so verify any quote they give against two other suppliers before committing.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing your price closer to what a manufacturer charges — since you resell rather than make these caps, we want to cut out the middleman margin and move toward the ₹0.65–0.80 range the market shows at our volume.
